newsitem.title: GERMANY: More German chemical sector talks set for March.
newsitem.headline: More German chemical sector talks set for March.

text.p: Discussions aimed at introducing lower wages in certain sectors of the German chemical industry will begin on a nationwide basis in mid-March, employers and unions said on Wednesday.

The discussions are aimed at finding a solution without any delay, the chemicals employers association and the chemical union IG Chemie said, but the two sides are disputing which specific areas of the industry will be affected by the cuts.

Employers are seeking lower wages in the plastics processing, chemicals fibres and caoutchouc (a type of rubber) processing sectors -- areas which employers maintain have been particularly badly hit by weakness in the German economy.
For their part, the unions say they do not want the caoutchouc processing area to be affected by the cuts.
Tyremaker Continental AG has said it and 26 other north German companies will if necessary start their own employers' association to ensure cheaper wages in the sector.
IG Chemie said the foundation of this breakaway group was unlikely and said a solution could be found within the current negotiating framework.
The proposed wage cuts are to be restricted to these specific areas, and the rest of the industry will come under wage agreements for the whole industry which were agreed late last year.
The accord reached for the 590,000 workers in the chemical industry includes a 1.5 percent pay rise for 1997 and maintains sick pay entitlements at 100 percent of salary.
